text.text: Cisco UCS for Big Data

graphic.text: Cisco UCS for Big Data

text.text: Big data has become mainstream as businesses realize its benefits, including improved operation efficiency, better customer experience, and more accurate predictions. However, companies are often challenged by the complexities of traditional server solutions. Big data solutions must enable high performance and scale as the business demands. To meet these requirements, Cisco designed a comprehensive solution: Cisco Common Platform Architecture (CPA), based on Cisco Unified Computing System (UCS) for big data.

text.text: Front View

graphic.text: Front View

text.text: Cisco Common Platform Architecture (CPA) for Big Data includes compute, storage, connectivity, and unified management features that enable rapid deployment, predictable performance, and reduced total-cost-of-ownership (TCO). Cisco CPA helps to meet your big data analytics needs while accelerating and streamlining integration with enterprise applications. Cisco CPA is based on Cisco Unified Computing System (UCS) which provides integrated, unified management enabling organizations to manage up to 10,000 servers and associated network infrastructure. This capability dramatically simplifies deployment and operational tasks.

text.text: Unified and Centralized Management Cisco UCS provides integrated management with Cisco UCS Manager and Cisco UCS Central Software, which enable organizations to manage clusters of up to 10,000 servers and associated network infrastructure, dramatically simplifying deployment and operational tasks.

text.text: Scalable and Predictable Performance Cisco CPA for big data, based on Cisco UCS, provides a framework for scaling linearly as processing needs grow without degrading performance or increasing management challenges and while continuing to deliver predictable and consistent performance.

text.text: Integration with Enterprise Applications The integrated architecture of Cisco UCS enables organizations to host both enterprise applications and big data applications in the same management domain, dramatically simplifies management, data center services, and data movement between applications.
